body.input: Which companies announced expanding into Finland in 2026?

response.content:
Here are notable companies that announced expansions into Finland in 2026:

## Major Tech / Data Center Investments

- **Google (Alphabet)** — In September 2026, Google announced its largest-ever European investment: at least €13 billion (~$15.1 billion) in AI infrastructure in Finland, including three new data centers and expansion of an existing facility across Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala. Google also signed a 22-year power purchase agreement with Finnish utility Fortum for the Loviisa nuclear power plant.

- **TikTok (ByteDance)** — TikTok announced a $1.16 billion investment to build a second data center in Finland, part of a broader €12 billion initiative to localize European user data.

- **atNorth** — In October 2026, the Nordic data center provider announced plans to develop a new data center (FIN05) in Salo, Finland, with an expected investment of approximately €2 billion.

- **Cerebras** — The AI chipmaker signed contracts for additional data center capacity in Norway and Finland during 2026, expanding its European footprint. Over 75% of its new data center capacity coming online in 2027 will be outside the U.S.

## Automotive / EV

- **GAC (Guangzhou Automobile Group)** — Launched its AION V electric vehicle in Finland as the first market in its collaboration with Inchcape, marking Finland as a pivotal entry point for GAC's pan-European EV strategy.

## Real Estate / Self-Storage

- **Heitman** (US real estate investment manager) — Acquired a majority stake in Finnish developer Talliosake's rental business and launched **Talli**, a Nordic drive-up self-storage platform, starting with 15 properties (11 in Finland) with plans to expand further across Finland and Sweden.

## Healthcare

- **SOL Group** (Italy) — Acquired Danish company **Nowus Healthcare** in mid-2026, enabling SOL Group (through its VIVISOL brand) to expand its respiratory care business into the Nordic countries, including Finland.

## Space / Incubation

- **ESA BIC Finland** — Expanded its business incubation operations to Finland's west coast (Vaasa) and Tampere, with Vaasa University and Turku Science Park establishing a new "West Coast Hub."

## Defence Industry

- Multiple **Ukrainian and Finnish defence companies** signed cooperation documents in 2026 covering unmanned aerial systems, ground vehicles, and uncrewed boats, as part of a new €300 million defence cooperation package between Ukraine and Finland.

These announcements reflect Finland's growing attractiveness as a destination for investment, particularly in data centers and AI infrastructure, driven by the country's cold climate, carbon-free power sources, and strategic Nordic location.

context.content: # Alphabet (GOOGL)’s Google Bets on Finland’s Cold Weather and Nuclear Power for its Next AI Buildout. (NASDAQ:GOOGL)'s Google will invest at least €13 billion, or about $15.1 billion, in AI infrastructure in Finland over the next two years, its biggest European investment, including three new data centers and a 22-year deal for up to 50% of the output of one of Finland's two nuclear power plants. The agreement with Finnish utility Fortum is Google's first nuclear energy deal outside the United States, and Fortum's stock jumped as much as 15.5% on the news, its biggest gain in Europe that day. Google plans to invest at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) in three new data centers and related infrastructure in Finland during 2027 and 2028. Google will purchase up to 50% of the electricity generated by Finland's Loviisa nuclear plant, providing a long-term source of low-carbon power for its data-center operations. Competition for Finland's power and data-center capacity could weaken some of the project's cost advantages.

context.content: 2. Best 0% APR Cards. # Google to invest €13 billion in Finland AI data centers. Google announced plans on Wednesday to pour at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) into AI infrastructure in Finland, a figure the company described as the single largest European investment in its history. The capital will be deployed in 2027 and 2028 across data centers and supporting infrastructure in Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala, the company said. During the construction phase, the investment is expected to contribute an average of €3.6 billion annually to Finland's GDP and support more than 37,000 jobs. As part of the announcement, Google signed a 22-year life extension power purchase agreement with Finnish energy company Fortum for the Loviisa nuclear power plant, which currently supplies roughly 10% of Finland's electricity and employs approximately 580 people. Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer of Alphabet and Google, said in a statement the investment "underscores Google's commitment to grow our presence responsibly, pairing the expansion of our technical infrastructure with new energy capacity, grid enhancements, and energy affordability initiatives.".

document.name: Google to invest €13 billion in Finland AI data centers

context.content: # Meet the data center capital of Europe as Google joins Microsoft and TikTok in betting over $30.2 billion on Finland. Data center expansion in the world is changing fast: while the U.S. boasts "data center alley" in Virginia and tax incentives for data center investment, Finland has rapidly come onto the scene as one of the largest data center magnets in Europe. But the latest and largest commitment came Wednesday, when Google announced its largest investment in Europe yet: an investment of at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) in AI infrastructure in Finland over the next two years. "This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," Google said in a statement. The data center project isn't the only investment Google is making into the country: it also signed an agreement with Finnish utility company Fortum to extend the life of a nuclear power plant in Loviisa in the company's latest attempt to use nuclear power as a clean energy source to power the data center investment.

context.content: # atNorth to develop new data center in Salo, Finland. *The planned site will support critical digital infrastructure while creating opportunities for local collaboration, energy partnerships and heat reuse.*. HELSINKI, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- atNorth, the leading Nordic high-density colocation and built-to-suit data center provider, today announced plans to develop a new data center FIN05, in Salo, Finland, as part of its ongoing objective to meet the demand for high performance digital infrastructure in a responsible way. Its proximity to Helsinki and Finland's digital talent pool also support the development of the site. atNorth's investment in the Salo site is expected to be approximately €2 billion. atNorth plans to enter into long-term power purchase agreements with local energy suppliers to support energy production in the region, as well as flexibility solutions that could support the efficient operation of Fingrid's transmission grid. FIN05 is part of atNorth's continued investment across the Nordics, alongside developments in Stockholm and Sollefteå in Sweden, Haugaland in Norway, Ølgod in Denmark and Kouvola Finland.

Talli will be led by Talliosake’s existing management team, with Talliosake retaining a minority stake in the business. Since 2010, the Finnish company has delivered more than 6,400 drive-up self-storage units across 230 properties in Finland and Sweden.  
  
The partnership marks a shift in Talliosake’s business model, which has traditionally focused on developing and selling individual self-storage units. Talli will instead adopt a develop-to-hold strategy, developing and operating income-generating properties for long-term ownership.  
  
Heitman and the management team plan to expand the platform across Finland and Sweden, targeting demand from both residential and business customers in what they describe as fragmented and undersupplied markets. [...] | New mandates/JVs and funds on the market | | | |
